# Garden Log April

## Sowings
The chitted potatoes went into the ground on 14 April, once the shoots were short and dark green and the soil had warmed enough to trust. I set them in rows about thirty centimetres apart with the shoots just below the surface, earthing up as I went so a late frost would not catch them. Two varieties went in, an early and a maincrop, in the bed that had held the beans last year. The carrots were the trickier job: I sowed them direct on 18 April when the soil read 12 C with the probe, because carrot seed sulks in cold ground and the roots fork if it is lumpy. I raked the bed fine, mixed the seed with a little dry sand to space it out, and watered the drill before covering rather than after, which keeps the seed from washing into clumps. Beyond those two, I started a tray of courgettes on the windowsill and a few leeks in a deep pot, both for planting out in late May. I also sowed a short row of radishes beside the carrots as a marker crop, since they come up fast and show me where the slower rows are. The salad leaves went into the raised bed under fleece, a cut-and-come-again mix that I can pick from in a few weeks. It was a full weekend of work and my back knew about it by Sunday evening. The beetroot went into a short double row beside the courgettes, and a single line of parsnips went into the deep bed where the roots can go down without hitting stones.

## Observations
The broad beans have picked up their first aphids, a cluster as thick as a thumbnail on the soft tips, so I pinched out the growing points to slow them down and left the rest for the ladybirds. The tomatoes have been hardening off for six days now, going outside in the morning and back under cover at dusk, and the stems have thickened up nicely. There are the first pea shoots showing through the mesh, pale and hooked, no taller than a matchstick yet. The potatoes are just breaking the surface, so the earthing up will need doing again within the week. Slugs have been busy around the salad bed despite the dry spell, so I have been out with the torch after dark. The soil in the second plot is still heavy and cold at depth, which is why the squash stays in its pot a while longer. The garlic left in from the autumn is standing tall and looks happy in the second plot. The fruit bushes are in full leaf and the first flowers have opened on the strawberries, so the netting went on to keep the birds off. The greenhouse is filling up fast and I have run out of bench space again, which happens every April and which I never seem to plan for.

## Notes
The last frost comes around 5 May in this spot, so nothing tender goes outside for good before then, however warm the days feel. I have the fleece ready and cut to size for the potatoes in case a cold snap arrives, and the cloches are stacked by the shed for the courgettes. If the temperature drops below about 3 C overnight I will cover the beans as well. Next jobs are to earth up the potatoes again, thin the carrots once they are large enough to handle, and harden off the leeks before they go to the second plot. I have made a note to check the soil temperature before sowing anything else direct, since the probe has saved me from more than one mistake this year. The fleece and the cloches live by the shed door now so they are easy to grab on a cold evening. If the frost does come late I will lose some of the tender things, but that is the gamble of an April planting.
